sec: Causes of anemia in CKD · p809

items.q: Anemia in CKD is described as:
Reduced RBC production is the lesser contributor to CKD anemia compared with raised RBC destruction.
opts: False — ↓ production is m/c and outweighs ↑ destruction
True — destruction is the m/c contributor
False — both contribute equally to the anemia
True, but only in dialysis patients
items.exp: ↓ RBC production (more common) >> ↑ RBC destruction (less common; ↓ red cell survival span). (Book p809)

items.q: The EPO defect in CKD anemia is described as:
opts: Inappropriately low EPO for the degree of anemia/hypoxia
EPO excess with high circulating ferritin
Excess EPO with receptor resistance at the marrow
Absent EPO synthesis in the peritubular cells
items.exp: ↓ EPO: inappropriately low EPO to the degree of anemia/hypoxia. (Book p809)

items.q: Under normal oxygen, the fate of HIF-α is:
items.exp: HIF-α pathway: normal O₂ → HIF-α degradation. (Book p809)

items.q: Under hypoxia, HIF-α pairs with HIF-β to drive:
items.exp: Hypoxia: HIF-α + HIF-β → erythropoietin production. (Book p809)

items.q: HIF-PH stands for HIF prolyl hydroxylase.
opts: False — it is HIF peroxynitrite hydrolase
True, but only in the medulla

items.q: The site of EPO production named in the flowchart is the:
opts: Peritubular interstitial fibroblasts in the cortex
Juxtaglomerular cells of the macula densa
Macula densa of the distal convoluted tubule
items.exp: Inappropriate production of EPO (site: peritubular interstitial fibroblasts in cortex > outer medulla). (Book p809)

items.q: Match the following cause of low iron to its detail — 1) Anorexia  2) Absorption  3) Blood loss … A) ↓ absorption  B) 1 ml = 0.5 mg Fe  C) Poor intake
items.exp: Low iron: anorexia, ↓ absorption, blood loss (1 ml = 0.5 mg Fe). (Book p809)

items.q: Each millilitre of blood loss represents how much iron?
items.exp: Blood loss: 1 ml = 0.5 mg Fe. (Book p809)

items.q: In anemia of chronic disease, inflammation drives production of:
items.exp: Inflammation: production of activin, CRP, interleukin → ↑ hepcidin → ↓ response to EPO. (Book p809)

items.q: The final step in that anemia-of-chronic-disease chain is:
Raised PTH causes anemia in CKD through:
items.exp: Raised PTH level → bone marrow fibrosis → anemia. (Book p809)

items.q: The deficiency causes listed under RBC production are:
items.exp: Deficiency: vitamin B₆, folic acid. (Book p809)

items.q: All but one are named in the note box about uremic toxins and RBC survival. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Note: uremic toxins are inhibitors of erythropoiesis; RBC glutathione depleted d/t ↓ survival; EPO effect ↑↑ after dialysis. (Book p809)

items.q: Uremic toxins act as inhibitors of erythropoiesis.
items.exp: Note: uremic toxins: inhibitors of erythropoiesis. (Book p809)

items.q: After dialysis, the EPO effect is:
items.exp: RBC glutathione depleted d/t ↓ survival; therefore EPO effect ↑↑ after dialysis. (Book p809)

items.q: A CKD patient has Hb 9.5 g/dl with a modest EPO level. The page's label for this EPO response is:
opts: Inappropriately low for the degree of anemia/hypoxia
Appropriately high for the degree of anemia
Receptor resistant with high circulating EPO
items.exp: ↓ EPO: inappropriately low EPO to the degree of anemia/hypoxia. (Book p809)
